name: Human Development throughout the Lifespan
subject: Social Sciences and Humanities
description: This course offers a multidisciplinary approach to the study of human development throughout the lifespan. Students will learn about a range of theoretical perspectives on human development. They will examine threats to healthy development as well as protective factors that promote resilience. Students will learn about physical, cognitive, and social-emotional development from the prenatal period through old age and will develop their research and inquiry skills by investigating issues related to human development.
prerequisites: Any university, college, or university/college preparation course in social sciences and humanities, English, or Canadian and world studies

overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of social-emotional development throughout the lifespan and of ways of influencing such development

specific_expectations.text: explain attachment theory as it relates to human development (e.g., with reference to the theories of John Bowlby, Mary Ainsworth, Kim Batholomew)
specific_expectations.text_html: explain attachment theory as it relates to human development (e.g., with reference to the theories of John Bowlby, Mary Ainsworth, Kim Batholomew)

elaborations.text: According to attachment theorists, why is infant attachment important?
elaborations.text_html: • According to attachment theorists, why is infant attachment important?

specific_expectations.text: describe the development of emotion throughout the lifespan (e.g., early emotions, stranger anxiety, emotional fluctuations, socioemotional selectivity)
specific_expectations.text_html: describe the development of emotion throughout the lifespan (e.g., early emotions, stranger anxiety, emotional fluctuations, socioemotional selectivity)

elaborations.text:
What are the first emotions that infants show?
  What differences might there be in the ways in which a teenage girl and an elderly woman express anger? What would account for these differences?
elaborations.text_html:
• What are the first emotions that infants show?
  • What differences might there be in the ways in which a teenage girl and an elderly woman express anger? What would account for these differences?

specific_expectations.text: describe ways in which parents and caregivers can promote secure attachment in infants and children (e.g., nurturing, responsive care, breastfeeding)
specific_expectations.text_html: describe ways in which parents and caregivers can promote secure attachment in infants and children (e.g., nurturing, responsive care, breastfeeding)

specific_expectations.text: explain the effects that secure and insecure attachment in the early years can have on social-emotional development in adolescence and adulthood
specific_expectations.text_html: explain the effects that secure and insecure attachment in the early years can have on social-emotional development in adolescence and adulthood

elaborations.text:
How does secure attachment in early life affect relationship building in later life?
  What types of behaviour and attitudes are characteristic of adults who have an anxious attachment style?
elaborations.text_html:
• How does secure attachment in early life affect relationship building in later life?
  • What types of behaviour and attitudes are characteristic of adults who have an anxious attachment style?

overall_expectations.title: Personality and Identity
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of various influences on personality development and identity formation throughout the lifespan
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of various influences on personality development and identity formation throughout the lifespan

specific_expectations.text: explain the process of identity formation throughout the lifespan (e.g., with reference to gender identity, ethnic identity, identity statuses)
specific_expectations.text_html: explain the process of identity formation throughout the lifespan (e.g., with reference to gender identity, ethnic identity, identity statuses)

elaborations.text:
How can families encourage the development of bicultural identity among its members?
  What circumstances can prompt role confusion in adolescence?
  What causes adults to go through identity reformulation?
elaborations.text_html:
• How can families encourage the development of bicultural identity among its members?
  • What circumstances can prompt role confusion in adolescence?
  • What causes adults to go through identity reformulation?

specific_expectations.text: explain how birth order and temperament can affect the development of an individual’s personality
specific_expectations.text_html: explain how birth order and temperament can affect the development of an individual’s personality

elaborations.text:
In what ways can sibling rivalry affect self-concept and the development of personality?
  What are the common personality traits of children who had an easy temperament in infancy? Of those who had a difficult temperament?
elaborations.text_html:
• In what ways can sibling rivalry affect self-concept and the development of personality?
  • What are the common personality traits of children who had an easy temperament in infancy? Of those who had a difficult temperament?

specific_expectations.text: analyse the relationship between personality and social interactions (e.g., the differences that introverted and extraverted people might experience in their social interactions; the impact on one’s personality of nurturing, supportive, empathetic interactions and critical, controlling ones)
specific_expectations.text_html: analyse the relationship between personality and social interactions (e.g., the differences that introverted and extraverted people might experience in their social interactions; the impact on one’s personality of nurturing, supportive, empathetic interactions and critical, controlling ones)

elaborations.text:
How might being in an abusive relationship affect an individual’s personality?
  In what ways might being a high achiever affect an individual’s interactions with colleagues or friends?
elaborations.text_html:
• How might being in an abusive relationship affect an individual’s personality?
  • In what ways might being a high achiever affect an individual’s interactions with colleagues or friends?

overall_expectations.title: Factors Affecting Social-Emotional Development
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of how factors affect social-emotional development, with an emphasis on the process of socialization
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of how factors affect social-emotional development, with an emphasis on the process of socialization

specific_expectations.text: analyse the role that family plays in socializing its members (e.g., with reference to the development of language, communication skills, confidence, competence, and self-esteem, and to the transmission of gender roles, culture, religion, and values such as respect for elders and for the environment)
specific_expectations.text_html: analyse the role that family plays in socializing its members (e.g., with reference to the development of language, communication skills, confidence, competence, and self-esteem, and to the transmission of gender roles, culture, religion, and values such as respect for elders and for the environment)

specific_expectations.text: analyse the effects of socialization on the social-emotional functioning of individuals throughout the lifespan (e.g., with respect to individuals’ values, behaviour, and sense of social responsibility; their ability to adjust to change, balance work and leisure, engage and communicate with other people and maintain relationships; their response to peer pressure, discrimination; the relationship between poor socialization and defiance, delinquency, and disengagement)
specific_expectations.text_html: analyse the effects of socialization on the social-emotional functioning of individuals throughout the lifespan (e.g., with respect to individuals’ values, behaviour, and sense of social responsibility; their ability to adjust to change, balance work and leisure, engage and communicate with other people and maintain relationships; their response to peer pressure, discrimination; the relationship between poor socialization and defiance, delinquency, and disengagement)

elaborations.text:
What have been some of the long-term effects of residential schools on the social-emotional functioning of First Nation children?
  What are some of the effects of isolation on the elderly?
  What trends have researchers found in the social-emotional functioning of adult men and women who grew up in homes where they witnessed their father batter their mother?
elaborations.text_html:
• What have been some of the long-term effects of residential schools on the social-emotional functioning of First Nation children?
  • What are some of the effects of isolation on the elderly?
  • What trends have researchers found in the social-emotional functioning of adult men and women who grew up in homes where they witnessed their father batter their mother?

specific_expectations.text: assess the impact of marginalization (e.g., marginalization related to factors such as age, poverty, disability, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, low literacy levels) on social-emotional development
specific_expectations.text_html: assess the impact of marginalization (e.g., marginalization related to factors such as age, poverty, disability, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, low literacy levels) on social-emotional development

elaborations.text:
How does the marginalization of people with disabilities leave them at higher risk for exploitation or victimization?
  Why do some societies disregard the skills, knowledge, and experiences of the elderly? What impact can this have on older people?
  What are the social-emotional benefits of a companion animal or animal-assisted therapy for elderly or disabled people?
